LESSON: WRITING 5.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING – NARRATIVE COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.1 Creative writing – Narrative composition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.3.1 Creative writing – Narrative composition, part of Strand 5 in Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we narrate events?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. take turns to narrate accounts of social events that they attended,

2. work jointly to outline key features of a narrative from a sample on a chart,

3. discuss features of a narrative,

4. compose a simple narrative about the theme of cultural diversity and read to peers for review,

5. keep the narrative created in the portfolio.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. take turns to narrate accounts of social events that they attended,
2. work jointly to outline key features of a narrative from a sample on a chart,
3. discuss features of a narrative,
4. compose a simple narrative about the theme of cultural diversity and read to peers for review,
5. keep the narrative created in the portfolio.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.3.1 Creative writing – Narrative composition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is developed as the learner embraces creative ideas to narrate an account of an event

attended

• Self-efficacy: This is developed as the learner effectively orders and prioritises events when composing a simple

narrative on the theme of cultural diversity.

Values:
• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner gives constructive comments during the review of each other’s narratives.

• Responsibility: This is cultivated as the learner participates in outlining features of a narrative and puts them on a chart.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural awareness is developed as the learner becomes informed about cultural diversity.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the skill of narrative writing to other languages like English and Kiswahili.
